Ila.note: Child of Vaivasvata Manu. Lived alternately as the woman Ila (mother of Pururavas by Budha) and the man Sudyumna, whose reign gave the sons below.

Manu.name: Vaivasvata Manu
Manu.note: Son of Surya Deva; progenitor of humankind in this age and father of Ikshvaku, first of the solar kings.

Ikshvaku.note: Son of Vaivasvata Manu; founder of the solar dynasty (Suryavamsha) and first king of Kosala at Ayodhya.

people.Mandhata: Born from his father Yuvanashva's side. Crying for milk, he was given Indra's own index finger to suck, the deva saying mam ayam dhasyati, he shall suck me: hence Mandhata. Emperor of all seven islands, from where the sun rises to where it sets. Also called Trasaddasyu, because thieves trembled at him. SB 9.6.33-37
people.Harishchandra: The king who kept his word past every ruin. Over him Vishvamitra and Vasishtha quarrelled so long that both were turned into birds and fought on as birds for years. Sonless, he begged a son of Varuna against the promise of sacrificing him. SB 9.7.7-8

Sagara.note: Born sa-gara, 'with poison', after his father's co-wife was fed poison while pregnant with him and he survived it. Reformed rather than killed the Yavanas, Shakas, Haihayas and Barbaras who opposed him. His sixty thousand sons by queen Sumati dug the ocean-trench searching for his stolen sacrificial horse, found it beside the meditating sage Kapila, and were burnt to ash in an instant for accusing him of the theft; only Amshuman, son of the other queen Keshini, survived to inherit and later win the horse back peaceably. SB 9.8.5-14

Asamanja.note: Wayward son of Sagara, exiled for his cruelty.

Amshuman.note: Grandson of Sagara who recovered the sacrificial horse; father of Bhagiratha.

Bhagiratha.note: Son of Amshuman; by fierce penance he brought the Ganga down from heaven to earth to redeem Sagara's sons, hence the river Bhagirathi.

Dilipa.name: Dilipa (Dirghabahu)
Dilipa.note: Dilipa II, also Dirghabahu, son of Khatvanga. The ideal king of Kalidasa's Raghuvamsha, whose service of the divine cow Nandini won him his son Raghu. SB 9.10.1

Raghu.note: Son of Dilipa; so glorious an emperor that the line is called the Raghuvamsha after him.

Aja.note: Son of Raghu; father of Dasharatha. Won Indumati, princess of Vidarbha, at her svayamvara over a hall of rival kings and devas; when a garland dropped by the passing sage Narada's quarrel killed her outright years later, his grief nearly killed him too, restrained only by the sage Vasishtha's counsel that a wise man's grief has a season and a season's end. Raghuvamsha 8.

Dasharatha.note: King of Kosala at Ayodhya; father of Rama by three queens. His promise to Kaikeyi sent Rama into exile and broke his own heart.

Rama.note: Eldest son of Dasharatha and Kausalya of the solar line. The eighteenth of the avatars, SB 1.3.22. By name — Ahalya released from her curse, Vishvamitra's yajna and the killing of Tataka and Subahu, breaking Shiva's bow at Sita's svayamvara, facing down Parashurama on the road home, fourteen years' exile with Sita and Lakshmana, Viradha, Surpanakha turned away and mutilated, Khara and Dushana destroyed, the golden deer Maricha and Sita's abduction, Jatayu's death defending her, alliance with Sugriva and the killing of Vali, Hanuman's leap and the search for Sita, the burning of Lanka, Setubandha, the war and Ravana's death, Sita's agni-pariksha, the coronation at Ayodhya, her later exile on rumour, Lava and Kusha raised at Valmiki's ashram unknowing, Sita's return into the earth, and Rama's own end walking into the Sarayu.

BharataR.name: Bharata
BharataR.note: Son of Dasharatha by Kaikeyi; he refused the throne his mother seized and ruled only as regent for Rama's sandals.

LakshmanaR.name: Lakshmana
LakshmanaR.note: Son of Dasharatha by Sumitra; Rama's devoted brother who followed him into exile and warred at his side. By name — fourteen years by Rama and Sita's side unasked, cutting off Surpanakha's nose and ears when she attacked Sita, drawing the Lakshmana-rekha Sita crossed to give alms to the disguised Ravana, wounded near-fatally by Indrajit's shakti weapon and revived by the Sanjeevani herb Hanuman carried whole, and killing Indrajit in the war's last stretch.

Shatrughna.note: Youngest son of Dasharatha by Sumitra, twin of Lakshmana; the slayer of the demon Lavana.

Lava.note: Son of Rama and Sita, born in the forest hermitage; twin of Kusha.

Kusha.note: Son of Rama and Sita, born in the forest hermitage; twin of Lava. Kusha and Lava sang the Ramayana before their father, not knowing him.

Chandraketu.note: Son of Lakshmana and Urmila (Lakshmana also had a son Angada, a namesake of the vanara prince).

Taksha.note: Son of Bharata and Mandavi; he gave his name to Takshashila.

SubahuR.name: Subahu
SubahuR.note: Son of Shatrughna and Shrutakirti; king of Mathura.

Atithi.note: Son of Kusha; a king of the Raghu line.

Nishadha.note: A king of Kosala descended from Rama.

people.Hiranyanabha: Disciple of Jaimini, master of the yoga of the mystics, and the teacher from whom Yajnavalkya received that yoga. SB 9.12.3-4
people.Maru: Perfected in yoga and living still, the Puranas say, in the village of Kalapa. At the end of the age of Kali he will begin the solar dynasty again. SB 9.12.5-6
people.Brihadbala: The last of the solar kings the Purana counts as past: he fought at Kurukshetra on the Kaurava side and was killed by Abhimanyu. He and Abhimanyu therefore stand on the same generation, which is what fixes the war's place in this whole tree. SB 9.12.8-9

Shanta.note: Daughter of Dasharatha and Kausalya, elder sister of Rama, given in adoption to King Romapada of Anga; wife of the sage Rishyasringa, whose rite granted Dasharatha his sons.

Shraddha.note: Wife of Vaivasvata Manu; mother of Ila and of the Manu sons who founded the earth's royal houses.

Sharyati.note: Son of Manu; his line held Anarta and Kusasthali (Dvaraka's site).

Nabhaga.note: Son of Manu; forebear of a solar branch. In one telling, away at his father's sacrifice when his brothers divided the inheritance without him, he was directed by his father to claim what the priests kept as their fee instead; the Angirasa priests, testing his honesty, gave him everything when he refused to take even that without their leave.

Nriga.note: Son of Manu; a king cursed to live as a lizard for a gift gone wrong.

Dishta.note: Son of Manu; forebear of the Vaishya kings.

Prishadhra.note: Son of Manu, made a shudra for slaying his guru's cow.

Anarta.note: Son of Sharyati; his realm Anarta held the coast where Dvaraka would rise.

Sukanya.note: Daughter of King Sharyati; devoted wife of the sage Chyavana. Struck his eyes by accident as a girl, mistaking them for fireflies in an anthill where he had sat motionless through long penance, and married him at her father's order to atone; when the Ashvin twins offered to make him young and beautiful if she chose correctly between three identical men, she picked her own aged husband by his eyes alone and stayed loyal, and Chyavana in turn taught the Ashvins the Soma sacrifice's own share, over Indra's objection.

Vikukshi.name: Vikukshi (Shashada)
Vikukshi.note: Eldest of Ikshvaku's hundred sons. Banished for eating a hare from the sacrificial offering, hence Shashada, the hare-eater; recalled to the throne at his father's death. SB 9.6.6-8

Puranjaya.name: Puranjaya (Kakutstha)
Puranjaya.note: Fought the demons for the devas mounted on Indra, who had taken the form of a bull: seated on its hump he is Kakutstha, and as the vehicle of Indra, Indravaha. SB 9.6.11-15

PrithuI.name: Prithu
PrithuI.note: Fifth of the solar kings. Not Vena's son Prithu, for whom the earth is named. SB 9.6.16

ChandraI.name: Chandra
ChandraI.note: Son of Vishvagandhi. Not Chandra Deva of the lunar line. SB 9.6.17

people.Shravasta: Built Shravasti Puri, the city that kept his name. SB 9.6.20

Kuvalayashva.name: Kuvalayashva (Dhundhumara)
Kuvalayashva.note: Killed the demon Dhundhu with twenty-one thousand sons at his side, and took the name Dhundhumara, slayer of Dhundhu. All but three of the sons burned in the fire the demon breathed. SB 9.6.21-24

people.Dridhashva: One of the three sons who survived Dhundhu's fire, with Kapilashva and Bhadrashva. SB 9.6.23-24

NikumbhaI.name: Nikumbha
NikumbhaI.note: Son of Haryashva. Not the rakshasa Nikumbha of Lanka. SB 9.6.24

YuvanashvaII.name: Yuvanashva
YuvanashvaII.note: A hundred wives and no son. The sages held an Indra-yajna for him in the forest; thirsty in the night he drank the consecrated water himself, and in time bore the child from his own right side. SB 9.6.25-32

people.Purukutsa: Given Narmada, sister of the Nagas, by her serpent brothers; she carried him down to Rasatala where, empowered by Vishnu, he killed the Gandharvas. Whoever remembers it is safe from snakes. SB 9.7.2-3; RV 6.20.10
people.Trasaddasyu: Bears his great-grandfather's epithet as his name. In the Rigveda he is called ardhadeva, half-god, a word used of no one else. SB 9.7.4; RV 4.42.8-9

Trishanku.name: Trishanku (Satyavrata)
Trishanku.note: Cursed by his own father into a chandala for carrying off a brahmin's bride at her wedding. Vishvamitra sent him bodily to heaven; the devas threw him back; Vishvamitra stopped him mid-fall, and he hangs there yet, head downward. SB 9.7.5-6

people.Rohita: The son promised to Varuna before his birth and deferred past every excuse; he took bow and arrows to the forest to stay alive, and came back six years later having bought Shunahshepha in his place. SB 9.7.9-20
people.Champa: Built Champapuri, which later became the capital of Anga. SB 9.8.1

Bahuka.name: Bahuka (Asita)
Bahuka.note: Driven out by his enemies, he died in the forest. His pregnant widow was poisoned by her co-wives but the child was born alive, carrying the poison: sa-gara. SB 9.8.2-5

DilipaI.name: Dilipa
DilipaI.note: Tried to bring the Ganga down to redeem Sagara's sons and died without succeeding. Not the Dilipa of the Raghuvamsha, who is four generations below Khatvanga. SB 9.9.1

people.Rituparna: King of Ayodhya, and the friend of Nala. He gave Nala the akshahridaya, the heart of the dice, and took from him the ashvavidya, the science of horses. Nala served in his kitchen and at his reins under the name Bahuka. SB 9.9.16-17; MBh 3.65-70

SudasaI.name: Sudasa
SudasaI.note: Not Sudasa of Panchala, nor the Rigvedic Sudas Paijavana of the Bharatas. SB 9.9.18

Saudasa.name: Saudasa (Kalmashapada)
Saudasa.note: Also Mitrasaha. Cursed by Vasishtha into a rakshasa; in that state he devoured a brahmin, and the widow cursed him to die at his next embrace. Twelve years sonless, he let Vasishtha beget his heir on his queen Madayanti. SB 9.9.20-38

people.Ashmaka: Carried for years and finally born when Vasishtha struck his mother's womb with a stone, ashman. SB 9.9.38

Balika.name: Balika (Mulaka)
Balika.note: Survived Parashurama's purge of the kshatriyas screened by a ring of women, hence Narikavacha, armoured in women; and because the kshatriyas began again from him, Mulaka, the root. SB 9.9.39-40

DasharathaI.name: Dasharatha
DasharathaI.note: Son of Balika, and not the father of Rama. SB 9.9.41

people.Khatvanga: Fought at the devas' side and won; offered a boon, he asked only how long he had to live, was told a few moments, left heaven at once and gave those moments entirely to Hari. SB 9.9.41-49
people.Vajranabha: Said to be born of the sun's effulgence. SB 9.12.2
people.Agnivarna: The last king the Raghuvamsha follows. SB 9.12.5

TakshakaI.name: Takshaka
TakshakaI.note: Son of Prasenajit. Not Takshaka the Naga who killed Parikshit. SB 9.12.7

people.Nimi: Second son of Ikshvaku. He would not wait for Vasishtha to finish Indra's sacrifice before beginning his own, and the two cursed each other's bodies to fall. From his preserved body, churned by the sages, Janaka was born. SB 9.13.1-11

AmbarishaM.name: Ambarisha
AmbarishaM.note: Son of Mandhata, and the most prominent of the three; accepted as son by his own grandfather Yuvanashva. Not Ambarisha the devotee, of Nabhaga's branch, whom Durvasa cursed. SB 9.7.1

people.Muchukunda: Son of Mandhata. He guarded the devas through a war of ages until Kartikeya came to relieve him, and when they offered him any boon but liberation he asked for sleep, and that whoever woke him should burn. He slept in a cave through the ages. Krishna led Kalayavana into that cave; Kalayavana kicked the sleeping man, and was ash before he understood. Then Muchukunda, who had lain down in his father's age, opened his eyes on Vishnu. SB 9.6.38, 10.51

HaritaM.name: Harita
HaritaM.note: With Ambarisha and Yauvanashva, one of the three most prominent in Mandhata's line. SB 9.7.1

MandhatriKanya.name: Mandhatri
MandhatriKanya.note: One of the fifty daughters of Mandhata and Bindumati. The Puranas name none of them individually, so she stands here for all fifty, who chose Saubhari together and then quarrelled over him, each certain he was hers alone. SB 9.6.38-44

HaryashvaAyodhya.name: Haryashva
HaryashvaAyodhya.note: King of Ayodhya, the first of the four to whom Madhavi was lent, and by her the father of Vasumanas. MBh 5.113

people.Vasumanas: Son of Haryashva of Ayodhya by Madhavi, renowned for giving; one of the four grandsons who lifted Yayati back to heaven. MBh 5.113, 5.118

Madayanti.note: Queen of Saudasa Kalmashapada. Her husband cursed to die at his next embrace, she bore his heir Ashmaka to Vasishtha by his own leave, and carried the child for years until Vasishtha struck her womb with a stone. Also called Damayanti in some recensions, and not to be confused with Damayanti of Vidarbha. SB 9.9.33-38

Sumati_3.name: Sumati
Sumati_3.note: First queen of Sagara, and mother of the sixty thousand who dug the ocean-trench and were burned to ash by Kapila. SB 9.8.8-13

Keshini.note: Second queen of Sagara, mother of Asamanjas, through whom the solar line continued. SB 9.8.14-16

AmbarishaN.name: Ambarisha
AmbarishaN.note: Son of Nabhaga, emperor of the world and the great devotee. Durvasa, offended over a broken fast, loosed a demon from his own hair at him; the Sudarshana chakra burned the demon and chased the sage through every world until he came back and begged pardon of the king he had wronged. Three sons: Virupa, Ketuman and Shambhu. SB 9.4-9.5, 9.6.1

people.Rathitara: Sonless; at his request the sage Angira begot sons in his wife's womb, and they were counted to both houses, Angirasa and Rathitara at once. SB 9.6.1-3

Sumati.note: Son of Nriga, in the line of Manu's sons. SB 9.2.17

VasuN.name: Vasu
VasuN.note: Son of Nriga; father of Pratika. Not Uparichara Vasu of Chedi, nor Vasu son of Jamadagni. SB 9.2.17

Pratika.note: Son of Vasu in Nriga's line; father of Oghavan. SB 9.2.17

Oghavan.note: Son of Pratika, and the last of Nriga's line the Purana names. His daughter Oghavati married Sudarshana. SB 9.2.17-18

Agnivesya.note: Youngest son of Narishyanta, also called Kanina and Jatukarnya; the brahmin gotra of the Agnivesyayanas descends from him. SB 9.2.21-22

Devadatta.note: Son of Narishyanta, and father of Agnivesya. SB 9.2.21

unions.note: The sons of Sudyumna (Ila’s male phase).
Their sixty thousand sons are counted, not named. SB 9.8.8
Ten sons at SB 9.2.20-21; the five carried here are those the Purana follows any further.
